a) find the value of $x$

Answers: a) $x=15\text{ cm}$

[Pedagogy audit v2 · Bridge] Question 10 gives an exterior angle on a straight line, which students have not met in any earlier question. A scaffolded question where they find the interior angle first and then use the angle sum would prepare them. It may sit better after Question 9, just before Question 10.
Proposed question: For this pair of triangles:
a) Find $\angle PRQ$.
b) Find $\angle XYZ$.
c) By using the angle sum of a triangle, decide if $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle XYZ$ are similar.
(with a diagram)
Answers: a) $\angle PRQ=55^\circ$; b) $\angle XYZ=40^\circ$; c) Yes. Both triangles have angles $40^\circ$, $55^\circ$ and $85^\circ$.
Comparison score: 42.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the difficulty jump gap (similarity-tests). Comparison score 52, between p8-q9 and p9-q10: The student must add the segments to get AB=12 and AC=15, notice the common angle at A, check the 1:3 ratios on the included sides, and name SAS. Nothing is signposted, but the steps are routine and there is a single decision path.
Proposed question: State, with reasons, why $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle ABC$ are similar.
(with a diagram)
Answers: SAS: $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{4}{12}=\frac{AE}{AC}=\frac{5}{15}=\frac13$ and the included angle $\angle DAE=\angle BAC$ is common, so $\triangle ADE\sim\triangle ABC$.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the difficulty jump gap (similarity-tests). Comparison score 61, between p8-q9 and p9-q10: The pair is hidden in an overlapping diagram. The student must find the common angle A and add segments to get AB = 12 and AC = 8. The pair is not the usual parallel-line configuration, because the correspondence is crossed (D↔C, E↔B). They must also choose SAS and write the vertex order correctly, with little scaffolding.
Proposed question: Two triangles in this diagram are similar.
Choose the appropriate test and write a similarity statement (e.g. $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FGH$).
(with a diagram)
Answers: $\triangle ADE\sim\triangle ACB$ by SAS: $\frac{AD}{AC}=\frac{AE}{AB}=\frac38$ and the included angle at $A$ is common.

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the difficulty jump gap (similarity-tests). Comparison score 52, between p8-q9 and p9-q10: Students choose a similar pair from three triangles and name the test. Part a needs sorted-side SSS matching. Part b needs cross-matching of the sides around 40° with a distractor triangle (DEF has the same side ratio but a 55° angle). The correspondence must be written in the right vertex order. This is about the level of p8-q9, a little harder because the correspondences are not signposted. It stays in the routine linked-procedure band.
Proposed question: For each set of three triangles, choose the two that are similar.
Choose the appropriate test and write a similarity statement (e.g. $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FGH$).
a) 
b) 
Answers: a) $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE$ by SSS: all three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.; b) $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GIH$ by SAS: two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles are equal.
